_about: Coordinator's diagnosis notes, written after each batch was scored (batch 1 and batch 2, 2026-10-16/17). They are post-hoc hypotheses, not tested, and the classification is the coordinator's own reading, not blind. mr_report.py appends them to SHIFTED_INSTANCES.md and FAILED_TO_TRANSFER.md. They never change a completed instance.
_batch1: All 21 shifted runs have the same form. The agent displays the gold's fault line, reads the gold in full and runs a test, then ranks the facade (the entry point the trigger test calls) first and the gold 2nd (17 runs), 3rd (3 runs) or 4th (1 run). No run ranks an intermediate hop first, no run fails to reach the gold, and no run times out. The shift rate follows the type of omission. It is high when the gold, without the omitted step, still reads as a complete routine for ordinary input: a plain sum with no NaN skip (Math-3 5/5, Chart-2 3/5), a high-surrogate match with no low-surrogate check (Lang-14 5/5), or a whitespace skip with no word-state reset (Lang-45 5/5). It is low when the omission leaves a visibly broken routine: a copy loop whose index never advances (Lang-39 0/5), an argmax that never records its index (Lang-16 1/5), or an accumulator returned without its fallback, so the result is null for every ordinary value (Lang-1 1/5). Lang-22 (1/5) falls between the two: the dropped loop bound is a cap that the gold's own javadoc states. Whether the gold's javadoc states the convention does not by itself separate the two groups, because Math-3's gold javadoc says 'sum of the finite entries' and it still shifted 5/5.
Lang-39: The method did not transfer. In all 5 counted runs the gold, ArrayUtils.replicate, was ranked first, and in 4 of them its fault line was displayed and it was read in full. The omission (`index += source.length;`) leaves a copy loop that writes every copy at index 0 and returns 0. Reading the loop makes the defect visible, and the trigger's symptom ("" for a repeat) points at a copy step that never advances. The facade lie (recursive halving) did not pull any counted run to the facade. An excluded run (run-005, a pre-registered contamination stop under W25) had the gold at rank 2; it is not counted. Diagnosis: a core-mechanics omission, which is the low-yield fault type. The instance stays as built (no redesign after results).
Lang-16: 1 of 5 runs shifted. The omission (`index = i;` in an argmax loop) leaves a loop that tracks the largest value but always returns the start index, a visibly incomplete idiom. Before any run, the builder's first design omitted `largest = array[i];` instead; it was replaced because a hop-3 edit could use the gold as an oracle (W24).
Lang-1: 1 of 5 runs shifted. The omission drops the long-range fallback, so the gold returns null for every value below the BigInteger threshold, against its own '@return ... not null'. The defect is visible both against the gold's javadoc and from the null result.
Lang-22: 1 of 5 runs shifted (run-002, gold rank 4, behind the facade, hop 1 and hop 2). The dropped `denom2 <= 10000` bound is a cap that the gold's own javadoc states ('the denominator of the fraction is at most 10,000'), so the gold can be checked against its own documentation.
Chart-2: 3 of 5 runs shifted. This is the special-value convention type (the NaN skip). The two unshifted runs ranked the gold first.
Math-3: 5 of 5 runs shifted, gold ranks 3, 3, 3, 2, 2. The facade, MathArrays.normalizeArray, was ranked first in every run. In the three rank-3 runs, hop 1 (BOBYQAOptimizer.rescaledEntries) sat between the facade and the gold.
Lang-14: 5 of 5 runs shifted, gold rank 2 each time, with the facade StringUtils.containsNone ranked first.
Lang-45: 5 of 5 runs shifted, gold rank 2 each time, with the facade WordUtils.initials ranked first.
_batch2: Batch 2 used the W26 preference for special-case omissions, yet only 5 of 10 instances shifted (17/50 runs), against 7 of 8 in batch 1. The 16 entry-point runs again ranked the facade first with the gold displayed and read in full. In three of them (Lang-7 runs 3 and 5, Closure-10 run 4) the ranking simply follows the call chain from the top (facade, hop 1 to hop 4, gold 6th). One Closure-10 run (run-003) never displayed the gold's fault line. Refined hypothesis across both batches: an instance shifts when the omission leaves NO LOCAL TRACE in the gold, and rarely shifts when it leaves one. A local trace is any of: (1) a parameter or local variable that is never read, or is written but never updated (Lang-32 `useTransients` never read; Lang-26 `locale` passed in but missing from the cache key; Lang-1 the computed `head` unused; Lang-16 `index` never updated; Lang-39 `index` never advanced); (2) a missing sibling case in an enumeration the gold visibly handles (Chart-11 SEG_QUADTO missing beside MOVETO/LINETO/CUBICTO; JacksonCore-5 `~1` missing beside `~0`; Lang-11 a `numbers`-only branch missing beside the `letters`-only branch); (3) a rule that the gold's own javadoc states (Lang-22's 10,000 cap). With this reading, all 9 no-trace instances shifted at least once (Lang-14, Lang-45, Math-3, Lang-7, Closure-10 5/5; Chart-2, Lang-30, Lang-63 3/5; Lang-15 1/5), and only 3 of the 9 traced instances did, each at 1/5 (Lang-1, Lang-16, Lang-22). This classification was made after seeing the results and must be tested prospectively.
Chart-11: 0/5. The omission removes the SEG_QUADTO coordinate count from a type dispatch that still lists MOVETO/LINETO and CUBICTO, so the missing sibling case is visible on reading. Local trace (2).
JacksonCore-5: 0/5. The gold decodes `~0` but no longer `~1`, the other half of the well-known JSON Pointer escape pair. Local trace (2).
Lang-11: 0/5. The usability cascade keeps `letters && numbers` and `letters` branches but has no `numbers` branch, so the `numbers` flag is only half used. Local trace (1)/(2).
Lang-26: 0/5. The cache key is built from dateStyle, timeStyle and timeZone, but not from the `locale` parameter that the method also uses. Not the preferred type (the builder recorded it as the only valid omission). Local trace (1).
Lang-32: 0/5. With the transient skip removed, the gold never reads its documented `useTransients` parameter. Local trace (1).
Lang-7: 5/5 (gold ranks 2, 2, 6, 2, 6). A minimum scan with no NaN check reads as an ordinary scan. In runs 3 and 5 the ranking lists the whole call chain from the facade down, with the gold 6th.
Closure-10: 5/5 (gold ranks 2, 2, 2, 6, 2). An identifier check without the reserved-word exclusion reads as complete. Run 3 never displayed the gold's fault line (GOLD_NOT_REACHED). In run 4 the ranking follows the call chain, with the gold 6th.
Lang-30: 3/5. A join loop without the null-element skip reads as an ordinary join.
Lang-63: 3/5. The milliseconds-width special case after seconds is gone; the rest of the formatter is intact and every flag is still read.
Lang-15: 1/5. The unbound-variable skip is removed; no parameter or variable goes unused. It is the one no-trace instance with a single shift.
_batch3: Batch 3 was built under the frozen no-local-trace rule (W29) and run in seven cost-guarded blocks. The pre-registered prediction reads SUPPORTED: 15 of 17 instances shifted at least once (s = 0.88, threshold 0.80), 61/85 runs (72%), against 12/18 instances and 38/90 runs (42%) in batches 1 and 2. Both W31 secondary subsets also read SUPPORTED: 14/15 when Lang-46 and Lang-65 are dropped (majority of 3 raters NO_TRACE), and 12/13 on the unanimous subset. Every shifted run ranked the facade first (61/61): the gold came 2nd in 54, 3rd in 1, 4th in 2 and 6th in 4, and the gold was read in full in 57. Caveats. Batch 3 differs from batches 1-2 in more than the rule: other bugs, older Lang versions, and a construction pipeline with a blind checker and one redesign. There is no control, so this is a prospective consistency check of the hypothesis, not a causal test. Five instances had a single shift in batches 1-2; in batch 3, Lang-57 had one and Lang-35 and Lang-51 two each.
Math-15: 0/5. The omission removes the middle tier (`a > 0.036 -> last = 6`) of a threshold ladder that chooses the length of a Taylor series, leaving tiers 8, 4 and 2. All three raters judged the gold NO_TRACE. The trigger fails on numerical accuracy, and the gold is the only method on the chain that approximates anything, so the symptom localises it. Hypothesis: on numerical code, an accuracy failure points to the approximating method whatever its local text shows.
Lang-65: 0/5. The omission removes `pos.setIndex(0);`, so one ParsePosition is reused across the patterns tried in turn. The authoritative checker said NO_TRACE; both extra raters said TRACE (T4 against 'parses the whole of the string', and T2 frozen position). The reused ParsePosition is a well-known Java pitfall that gpt-5.5 recognised in every run. This is the one batch-3 instance whose robustness majority was TRACE, and it did not shift.
Lang-46: 4/5. The other instance whose two extra raters said TRACE (T3). It still shifted in 4 of 5 runs.
Lang-58: 5/5 (gold ranks 2, 6, 2, 6, 6), after a pre-run redesign for a T3 trace. In the rank-6 runs the ranking lists the call chain from the facade down.
Lang-53: 5/5 (gold ranks 3, 2, 4, 2, 4). The facade was ranked first in every run, with hops between it and the gold in three runs.
Lang-57: 1/5. The only batch-3 instance with a single shift.
